terms.gloss: dragon fruit: the climbing cactus that bears it (the botanical name)
terms.comment: The botanists’ name of the plant, labelled modern; the fruit is pōmum Selēnicēreī. It was long called Hylocēreus undātus. No reference work we searched (Traupman, Morgan–Owens, Levi–Bini) has a name for it, and we have not Latinised the local one.

terms.grammar: pōmum, pōmī n., with the genitive of dracō, dracōnis m.
terms.comment: A plain rendering of ours of the name the fruit has in English and in Indonesian (buah naga), for the table, where the botanical name is too long to say.

phrases.latin: Pōmum Selēnicēreī intus album est, minūtīs sēminibus nigrīs sparsum.
phrases.english: A dragon fruit is white inside, dotted with tiny black seeds.

phrases.latin: Hoc pōmum rubrum Selēnicēreī est; per medium id secābō.
phrases.english: This red fruit is a dragon fruit; I’ll cut it down the middle.

phrases.latin: Vīn' pōmum dracōnis? Intus album est, sēminibus nigrīs sparsum.
phrases.english: Would you like some dragon fruit? It’s white inside, dotted with black seeds.
